Quant hedge funds rely on a mix of statistical and mathematical models to identify alpha and manage risk. Core tools include linear and multiple regression models for factor exposure and prediction, ARIMA and GARCH models for time-series forecasting and volatility clustering, Kalman filters for state estimation in dynamic systems, and cointegration tests such as Engle-Granger or Johansen for pairs trading. Portfolio construction often uses mean-variance optimization, Black-Litterman, and risk-parity frameworks, while risk is measured with Value at Risk (VaR), Expected Shortfall, and Monte Carlo simulation. More advanced firms apply machine learning models including random forests, gradient boosting, support vector machines, and deep neural networks for signal extraction, alongside hidden Markov models and regime-switching models to detect market states.
